description:
77 Stoke Newington Church St was used as a social housing/bedsit, while the use class remained C3(dwellinghouse). This application seeks planning permission and listed building consent for internal alterations to sensitively restore the property's historic character while restoring it for sustainable, modern single family use. The works focus on reinstating the original plan form by removing later partitions where sensible, restoring historic features such as fireplaces, cornicing, shutter boxes, and floorboards, and introducing traditionally designed joinery and fittings throughout.

Non-original elements, including built-in cupboards and outdated kitchens and bathrooms, will be removed or reconfigured. New kitchens, bathrooms, and storage will be introduced in discreet locations using existing service routes where possible, minimising disruption to the building fabric. A new ensuite and utility area will be incorporated on the upper floors to support contemporary living needs.

All existing windows—non-historic and dating from mid-to-late 20th century—will be refurbished or replaced with timber slimline double-glazed units, improving energy performance while respecting the building's appearance. Historic staircases and flooring will be repaired and restored, with sympathetic new finishes applied throughout.
decision_conditions:
The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.


REASON: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.

The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

<p>Unless otherwise hereby approved, all new works in respect of all the works hereby approved (and any other incidental works to be carried out in this connection) shall match the existing building in respect of materials used, detailed execution and finished appearance.

</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To ensure a satisfactory external appearance and safeguard the significance of the heritage asset.</p>

<p>Any new plant shall be installed, together with any associated ancillary equipment, so as to prevent the transmission of noise and vibration into neighbouring premises. The rated noise level from all plant and ancillary equipment shall not increase the existing background noise level (10dB below) when measured 1m external from the nearest residential or noise sensitive premises. An assessment of the expected noise levels shall be carried out by a suitably qualified (IOA accredited) and experienced acoustic consultant, in accordance with BS 4142:2014+A1:2019 ‘Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound,’ and any mitigation measures necessary to achieve the above required noise levels shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in writing for approval.</p><p>The plant shall thereafter be installed and maintained in accordance with the approved details.</p><p>Reason: To safeguard the amenity of the area in respect of noise and disturbance.</p>
